posts.title: How do you beat the 6:50 Scorned Wilderness world record? A route you can run with
posts.html:
The 6:50 is TexasPete's 6:50.000 run of the Scorned Wilderness raid, the number one time on the speedrun.com Raid board (version 1.0.0.6+). You beat it by combining Nanobit's 1.0.1 route with Dotxy's 1.0.1.2 flight and playing the five splits at the community-best pace.

This series teaches every step, in the order you need it. It is a route you can run with.

Is the 6:50 beatable today?

The 6:50 is beatable on today's patch. TexasPete played the record on 14 October, "prior to the windstep double jump and some other new routing strats" (6:50 description). Since then Dotxy has found a way to fly through Kuldra's Sanctum, and FastTipsGaming has shown a Stronghold launch with no Thane kill. Built only from pieces that still work on 1.0.1.2, the frame-timed run path adds up to 6:52.80, and the target pace is 6:48.10, with the extra seconds coming from the Sanctum flight, the heart safespot and the Keep.

Nanobit gives the verdict on the current route: "clearly can be done sub 7 judging by my sum of best, but needs very clean movement and strong zoops" (7:01 description).

What is the Scorned Wilderness raid speedrun?

The Scorned Wilderness raid is the end-game raid of RuneScape: Dragonwilds (a chain of floating islands that ends at Kuldra, the God-Eater). The speedrun.com Raid category times it from the loading screen to the escape:

"Timer starts the first frame the loading icon disappears going into the raid. Timer ends on the frame the screen goes black after the "Get out now!" timer ends after defeating Kuldra's Heart." (speedrun.com rules)

The run has five splits, each ending at an extraction point:

Split Area TexasPete 6:50 Nanobit 7:01
1 Dragontail Vines 81.52 s 87.82 s
2 Fragments of Ghornfell 61.10 s 67.10 s
3 The Shattered Stronghold 51.70 s 63.10 s
4 Cataclysm Keep 96.30 s 87.80 s
5 Kuldra's Sanctum 119.38 s 116.15 s

Segment times are measured frame by frame from each video (±0.1 s), as explained in Where is the 6:50 won?.

Where does the board stand?

# Runner Time Patch Video
1 TexasPete 6:50.000 1.0.0.6+ (pre-1.0.1 strats) watch
2 Nanobit 7:01 1.0.1 / 1.0.1.1 watch
3 Nimblesk 8:28 1.0.0.6+ watch
4 ChiefWes 9:43 1.0.0.6+ watch

The board was read on 3 November 2026 with zero runs awaiting verification. The bracket covers every patch from 1.0.0.6 onward, so a run on 1.0.1.2 ranks directly against the 6:50.

How is the series organised?

The six pillars follow the order a runner meets each problem. Start at Pillar 1 if you have never entered the raid. Start at Pillar 3 if you already run sub-10.

  1. Get raid-ready: every level, spell, item, quest and setting, and how to get each one.
  2. The route, split by split: the 1.0.1.2 route in play order, every skip credited to its finder.
  3. Movement tech: zoops, dive cancels, infinite double jumps and Surge dashes.
  4. Practice and consistency: drills and reset habits that land every skip every attempt.
  5. Data and the record: frame-measured splits, the sum of best and the pace that beats 6:50.
  6. Patch watch: what each patch changed, quoted from Jagex, and the rules that decide what counts.

Who found the tech?

The series stands on the community's discoveries, and every post credits the finder by name:

  • Dotxy: the dive cancel, the infinite double jump and Sanctum flight.
  • SectorTSWG via Sir_Rebral: the skip to Fragments of Ghornfell.
  • Sir_Rebral: the Garou Thane kill through the gate.
  • IINo1goodII and notmusty1: the hole in Cataclysm Keep.
  • SamFPlays: the Surge + Phase Dash combo and the follow-along route.
  • Zilko, CrossRSDW and FastTipsGaming: the Kuldra fight skips.
  • wes7918 (ChiefWes): the rib clip at Kuldra's checkpoint.
  • Nanobit and TexasPete: the records, the zoops and the run notes this series measures.

What this means when you run

  • Learn the movement kit first; every skip on today's route is built from five primitives.
  • Run to the split targets 1:22.70, 2:23.20, 3:15.70, 4:42.30 and 6:48.10: level with the 6:50 through split 3, about 8 s ahead after the Keep.
  • Spend your practice hours in the Sanctum, the swing segment: bring Dotxy's 51.9 s flight down to the 49.0 s target.

  • Nanobit: "clearly can be done sub 7 judging by my sum of best, but needs very clean movement and strong zoops" (7:01 description)
  • Nanobit: "It's a great run but it is using some strats that have been patched at this point." (7:01 description)

  • The 6:50 was played on a route that patch 1.0.1 has since changed, so today's record attempt runs a newer route.

posts.title: What do you need to speedrun the Scorned Wilderness raid?
posts.html:
Raid-ready is the state where your character owns every unlock the record route uses before the timer starts: the Agility movement kit, three spells, one combat perk, a short list of consumables and the quest gate that opens the raid.

This pillar turns that list into five short posts. Each one names the requirement, the level or cost, and how to get it, with the source quoted.

Why do requirements come first?

Every skip in the current route is built from unlocks. The Fragments zoop uses Air Dash, the Abyssal Demon skip uses Surge and Phase Dash, and Dotxy's Sanctum flight uses Windstep, the Jump Attack and a targeted AoE spell on your ring.

The wiki states the rule for the whole kit: Agility "unlocks the whole movement kit: Windstep, Double Jump, Air Dash, Phase Dash and Recall" (Agility, wiki). Level the character first, then learn the route.

What is on the requirement list?

Requirement Level or cost Used for Post
Quest gate Icthlarin's Little Helper complete, Regicide started Entering the raid 02
Windstep Agility 5 (infobox: 8), 5 Air runes Air vent, Thane door, flight 03
Double Jump Agility 10 Infinite double jump, zoops 03
Air Dash Agility 32 Soulscourge and necro skips 03
Phase Dash Agility 44, 20 Air + 10 Astral Demon skip, weak-zoop recovery 03
Recall, Reactive Recall Agility 57, 70 Practice safety net 03
Surge Magic 11, 10 Astral + 10 Law Demon skip, Kuldra approach 04
Jump Attack Attack 25 perk Death From Above! Dive cancel, flight 04
Targeted AoE spell Magical Mending (Artisan 56), or Superheat (Artisan 20) Dive cancel, flight 04
Runes Runecrafting 1 Air, 3 Astral, 15 Earth, 38 Nature, 50 Law (wiki) Every spell above 04
Enfeeble Magic 61 Heart phase 04
Fleet-footed Infusion 1 Clean Water + 1 Feathers The whole run 05
Strong Tea, mace, 2H staff, mage armour Crafted or best owned Thane kill, Heart 05
Rest, hydration, bed, keybinds, splits Pre-run setup Every attempt 06

Which posts are in this pillar?

  1. How do you unlock the Scorned Wilderness raid? The quest gate, the entrance and Rasthin's Rest.
  2. Which Agility levels do you need for raid skips? Windstep to Reactive Recall, with costs and training.
  3. Which spells and perks do raid skips use? Surge, Tempest Shield, Enfeeble, the Jump Attack and the AoE spell.
  4. What gear and consumables should you bring? SamFPlays' gear list with recipes.
  5. What should you set up before every raid attempt? Rest, hydration, respawn, keybinds and the split file.

Where does each unlock land on a fresh account?

The Raid Lab Hardcore 1 to Max route places every unlock in a phase, and the build sheets in the Raid Lab repo follow the same order:

Phase Region Unlocks for the raid
0 Temple Woods Windstep, Double Jump, Air runes (Rune Mysteries), Leggings of Lightness
2 Ghornfell Tempest Shield, Surge, Air Dash, Superheat (Artisan 20)
3 Fellhollow Phase Dash, Magical Mending (Artisan 56)
4 Dowdun Reach Recall, Death From Above! (Attack 25, placed between Attack 11 and 30)
5 Umbral Sands Reactive Recall, Enfeeble, Icthlarin's Little Helper complete
6 Scorned Wilderness Regicide started, Fleet-footed Infusion, Strong Tea

Law runes are the one source conflict. The wiki states "Law runes can be crafted at a rune altar at level 50 Runecrafting or higher" (Law Rune, wiki), while the Hardcore route lists Runecrafting 16. Check it in-game, and stock up from Garou Packs, which drop 5 to 10 Law runes at a 10/100 rate (Garou Pack, wiki).

Which build should you follow?

The Raid Lab publishes four builds, each with its stats, items, ring loadout, keybinds and pre-run state:

Build For Status
1.0.1.2 record route (flight) PC runners going for sub-6:50 Theory: Nanobit's 7:01 route plus Dotxy's flight; no posted run uses it yet
Console 1.0.1.2 route PlayStation and Xbox Works: FastTipsGaming's full unedited raid, 2 November
Safe learning route New runners, one skip at a time SamFPlays' 1.0.1 follow-along; re-test Vines to Keep on 1.0.1.2
Hardcore-safe route One-gravestone characters Repo plan with Reactive Recall always on

Start on the safe learning route, then move to the record route once the zoops and the flight loop land on demand.

What this means when you run

  • Reach Agility 44 and Magic 11 before your first timed attempt.
  • Put Magical Mending on your ring and unlock Death From Above! at Attack 25.
  • Pack a Fleet-footed Infusion every single run.

  • SamFPlays: "Fleet Foot Infusion: MUST BRING. Cuts sprinting stamina cost by 50%." (Every Skip Explained, Gear & setup, 1:43)

posts.title: How do you unlock the Scorned Wilderness raid?
posts.html:
The raid gate is the quest requirement that opens the Scorned Wilderness: complete Icthlarin's Little Helper and start Regicide. With that done, the raid entrance in the north-western Fractured Plains of Ghornfell takes you to Rasthin's Rest, the hub where every run begins.

This post gets you from quest log to first timer start.

What do you need?

Term What it means
Icthlarin's Little Helper Main-story quest; complete it.
Regicide The next main-story quest; start it.
Rasthin's Rest The raid hub and the only place you can build.
Commander Zilyana The NPC who starts or resumes a run.
Zilyana Teleporter The extraction point at the end of each segment.

The wiki lists the gate as "Complete Icthlarin's Little Helper; start Regicide" and the entrance as "North-western Fractured Plains, Ghornfell" (Scorned Wilderness, wiki). speedrun.com tracks both quests as Primary Quest values on its Any% board, so they sit on the main story line (speedrun.com).

How do you get in?

  1. Finish Icthlarin's Little Helper in the main quest line. Its final step is defeating Fuzan in the Umbral Sands (Icthlarin's Little Helper, wiki).
  2. Start Regicide at the Dragon Gate: the wiki's start is "Interact with the Dragon Gate north of the Fractured Plains." (Regicide, wiki).
  3. Go through to the Scorned Wilderness from the north-western Fractured Plains in Ghornfell.
  4. Arrive at Rasthin's Rest, the hub.
  5. Set your bed spawn here and sleep before your first attempt (setup checklist).
  6. Talk to Commander Zilyana to start a new run. The speedrun timer starts on the first frame the loading icon disappears.

How does Rasthin's Rest work?

Rasthin's Rest is the safe hub at the raid's edge. Jagex added it with 1.0 as "a new area which players can build in, and the Raid area which does not permit building, because of the big dragon" (1.0 notes, Steam).

Commander Zilyana starts or resumes runs, and raid deaths place your gravestone near her (Rasthin's Rest, wiki). Since 1.0.0.5, "Summon Shelter will be able to be used in the Scorned Wilderness hub" (1.0.0.5 notes), so you rest right at the start line.

What are the five splits?

Each raid segment ends at a Zilyana Teleporter, the extraction point that saves your progress. The community split file uses the five segments:

  1. Dragontail Vines
  2. Fragments of Ghornfell
  3. The Shattered Stronghold
  4. Cataclysm Keep
  5. Kuldra's Sanctum

Splits 1 to 4 end on the "Extraction point unlocked" banner. Split 5 ends on the cut to black after "Get out now!" (speedrun.com Raid rules).

What this means when you run

  • Start Regicide once, then the raid stays open for every attempt.
  • Set your bed at Rasthin's Rest so every respawn lands at the start line.
  • Split on the extraction banner for segments 1 to 4 and on the cut to black for segment 5.

  • The Scorned Wilderness speedrun route

  • Wiki: Requirement "Complete Icthlarin's Little Helper; start Regicide"; Entrance "North-western Fractured Plains, Ghornfell" (Scorned Wilderness)
  • Jagex, 1.0: "Added the Scorned Wilderness region." (Steam)
  • Jagex, 1.0.0.5: "Summon Shelter will be able to be used in the Scorned Wilderness hub." (Steam)
  • speedrun.com Raid rules: "Timer starts the first frame the loading icon disappears going into the raid." (speedrun.com)

posts.title: Which Agility levels do you need for raid skips?
posts.html:
Agility is the skill that owns the movement kit in RuneScape: Dragonwilds. Jagex added it in 0.12.1, built "to make you faster, leaner and meaner" (0.12.1 notes, wiki), and every 1.0.1+ raid skip uses at least one of its unlocks.

Train Agility to 44 for the full route and to 70 for a safety net while you practise.

Which unlocks does the route use?

Level Unlock Cost Cooldown Raid use
5 Windstep 5 Air runes 3 s Air vent, Thane door, flight start
10 Double Jump 10 stamina none Infinite double jump, zoops
22 Hopper passive none Cheaper jumps
32 Air Dash stamina not listed Soulscourge and necro skips
35 Breakfall passive none Softer landings
44 Phase Dash 20 Air + 10 Astral 45 s Demon skip, weak-zoop recovery
57 Recall 30 Air + 15 Law 75 s Practice safety net
70 Reactive Recall upgrade to Recall uses the Recall tether Fatal falls teleport you back

Values come from the wiki's Agility table and spell pages (Agility).

What does Windstep need?

Windstep is the spell that makes you jump up to 16 metres and fall more slowly, with a 7-second window to use it after casting (Windstep, wiki). It is the first input of Dotxy's flight loop and of Sir_Rebral's Thane-door windjump.

The sources give two levels. The Agility unlock table lists Agility 5; the Windstep infobox shows level 8, carried over from its Runecrafting days. Jagex moved it in 0.12.1: "Windstep is now an Agility skill spell, rather than a Runecrafting skill spell." (0.12.1 notes, Steam). Reach Agility 8 and both readings are covered.

Leggings of Lightness make Windstep cost zero runes (gear post).

What do Double Jump and Hopper add?

Double Jump is a second jump in mid-air, up to 4 metres, with no cooldown and the same 10 stamina as a normal jump (Double Jump, wiki). Dotxy's infinite double jump chains it after every Jump Attack cancel. Hopper at 22 makes each jump cheaper.

What does Air Dash add?

Air Dash is the 10-metre horizontal dash you get by pressing evade while airborne (Air Dash, wiki). Nanobit counts them in his run notes: "Can do 4 air dash instead of 3 towards 1st air anima pillar" (7:01, 0:51).

What does Phase Dash add?

Phase Dash grants extra Air Dashes while airborne, up to 3 per cast, for 20 Air + 10 Astral runes on a 45-second cooldown (Phase Dash, wiki). SamFPlays pairs it with Surge to clear the Abyssal Demon (Phase Dash & Surge combo, 0:00). Nanobit spends it like a budget: "then you can save the phase dash for Kuldra" (7:01, 5:18).

What do Recall and Reactive Recall add?

Recall places a runic marker; recast to teleport back. At Agility 70, Reactive Recall fires automatically on a fatal fall and consumes the tether (Reactive Recall, wiki). Use it in practice to retry a vertical skip at once. The 0.12.1 notes keep Breakfall honest: "Fatal falls will still kill you though."

How do you train Agility?

  1. Sprint everywhere. The wiki lists foot travel, courses, dodging vault traps and dodging enemy attacks as XP sources (Agility).
  2. Run the agility courses in each region as you pass them.
  3. Follow the phase order: Windstep and Double Jump in Phase 0, Air Dash in Phase 2, Phase Dash in Phase 3, Recall in Phase 4, Reactive Recall in Phase 5 of the Raid Lab Hardcore route.

Travel on foot pays more as you level. The wiki: "Players will gain 50/200/400 Agility XP at level 1/48/85, passively simply by running on foot across the world." (Agility, wiki). The Brynmoor courses open at Agility 1, so the first course is available from your first hour.

Fund the runes as you train. Windstep and Phase Dash use Air runes (Runecrafting 1) and Phase Dash adds Astral runes (Runecrafting 3). Recall adds Law runes: the wiki states "Law runes can be crafted at a rune altar at level 50 Runecrafting or higher" (Law Rune, wiki), while the Hardcore route lists Runecrafting 16. Check the Law altar level in-game, and collect Law runes from Garou Packs (5 to 10 at a 10/100 rate) in the meantime (Garou Pack, wiki).

What this means when you run

  • Hit Agility 44 so Phase Dash is ready for the Abyssal Demon and the Kuldra approach.
  • Count your dashes per gap the way Nanobit does, and save Phase Dash for the end.
  • Practise with Reactive Recall at Agility 70 so missed vertical skips cost seconds.

Sources

  • Jagex, 0.12.1: "Windstep is now an Agility skill spell, rather than a Runecrafting skill spell." (Steam)
  • Wiki unlock table and spell pages: Agility, Windstep, Phase Dash, Recall
  • Wiki: "Players will gain 50/200/400 Agility XP at level 1/48/85, passively simply by running on foot across the world." (Agility)
  • Wiki: "Law runes can be crafted at a rune altar at level 50 Runecrafting or higher." (Law Rune)
  • Nanobit: "Can do 4 air dash instead of 3 towards 1st air anima pillar" (7:01, 0:51)
  • Nanobit: "Sometimes this zoop is strong enough to only need 1 dash, then you can save the phase dash for Kuldra." (7:01, 5:18)

posts.title: Which spells and perks do raid skips use?
posts.html:
Raid spells and perks are the Magic, Attack and Artisan unlocks the route casts on top of Agility: Surge for long dodges, the Death From Above! Jump Attack with Magical Mending as the cancel spell for Dotxy's cancels, Tempest Shield as a panic button and Enfeeble for the Heart.

Three of them are mandatory: Surge, the Jump Attack and a targeted AoE cancel spell.

Which spells and perks matter?

Unlock Level Cost Cooldown Raid use
Surge Magic 11 10 Astral + 10 Law 45 s Abyssal Demon skip, Kuldra approach
Jump Attack (Death From Above!) Attack 25 perk 15 stamina none listed Dive cancel, infinite double jump, flight
Magical Mending (cancel spell) Artisan 56 20 Earth + 10 Nature 60 s The cast you cancel in the dive cancel
Superheat (lower option) Artisan 20 5 Air + 15 Fire 10 s Alternative cancel spell
Tempest Shield Attack 11 15 Air 45 s Blocks all damage while held
Enchant Weapon: Air (optional) Attack 30 15 Air + 5 Astral 90 s Faster Garou Thane kill
Enfeeble Magic 61 20 Water + 20 Astral 75 s Heart phase

Values come from the wiki spell pages, cited below.

Which runes do you need?

Rune Runecrafting level (wiki) Feeds
Air 1 Windstep, Phase Dash, Tempest Shield, Superheat
Astral 3 Surge, Phase Dash, Enfeeble
Earth 15 Magical Mending
Fire 25 Superheat
Nature 38 Magical Mending
Law 50 Surge, Recall

Law runes carry a source conflict. The wiki states "Law runes can be crafted at a rune altar at level 50 Runecrafting or higher" (Law Rune, wiki); the Raid Lab Hardcore route lists Runecrafting 16. Check the altar in-game. Garou Packs drop 5 to 10 Law runes at a 10/100 rate (Garou Pack, wiki), which keeps Surge stocked while you level.

Rune totals per run are a count you make yourself. Count your casts in one clean practice run and stock double that.

What does Surge do?

Surge is a Magic spell that gives three long dodges of 8 metres each, with the charges lasting two minutes (Surge, wiki). SamFPlays built the Phase Dash and Surge combo on it: "click that like whatever your dash button is to activate surge. At the end when your momentum starts to die, jump and then double dash." (Every Skip Explained, 0:58).

Since 1.0 you cast Surge while moving: "you can now move while casting a range of spells, including Enchant Weapon, Windstep and Surge" (1.0 notes, Steam).

What is the Jump Attack?

The Jump Attack is the plunging melee attack unlocked by the Attack perk Death From Above! at Attack 25 (Death From Above!, wiki). Jagex describes the trigger in 1.0.1: "above the max height of the double jump's arc from the ground, inputting an attack will plunge you downward to slam into unfortunate victims below... And yes, Windstep counts here." (1.0.1 notes, Steam).

Hold a melee weapon with a plunge animation. Nanobit warns: "remember that DScim doesn't have a plunge animation, so you need something else equipped" (7:01, 5:07). Jagex's 1.0.1.2 notes "Fixed an issue where the Dragon Scimitar would not allow users to Jump Attack in certain circumstances", so test the Dragon Scimitar's plunge in-game before you carry it as your only melee weapon.

Why is Magical Mending the cancel spell?

The cancel spell is the targeted AoE cast that Dotxy's dive cancel interrupts: "instantly exit the jump attack animation and ending lag by casting a targeted AOE spell, cancel the cast to gain full movement over your character instantly" (Dive Cancel, description). Any targeted AoE spell works, and the community default is Magical Mending. FastTipsGaming: "Everyone pretty much agrees that magical mending is the best one to use because most people unlock it earlier than the others." (Infinite Jump, 0:17).

Superheat at Artisan 20 is the lower option, and it sits on Dotxy's own ring in his flight video (Sanctum flight, 0:07). Whether a cancelled cast spends runes or starts the cooldown is a test step: cast-and-cancel ten times and watch your rune count.

Which ring slots do the runners use?

Spell Ring slot Source
Cancel spell Slot 1 (Q 1) Nanobit
Surge Slot 3 (Q 3) loopuleasa
Phase Dash Slot 4 (Q 4) loopuleasa
Windstep Slot 7 (Q 7) Nanobit

Nanobit: "I'm using Q1E for the plunge-cancel tech, and Q7 a lot of the time to windstep." (reply on the 7:01). Full keybinds are in the setup checklist.

What do Tempest Shield and Enfeeble add?

Tempest Shield "prevents all damage while blocking, including normally unblockable attacks" for 15 Air runes at Attack 11 (Tempest Shield, wiki). It is the safety option on the hardcore-safe build.

Enfeeble at Magic 61 weakens the target's attacks; the wiki page is a stub with no effect size (Enfeeble, wiki). The Raid Lab requirement list attaches it to the Heart phase.

When do you unlock each one?

On the Raid Lab Hardcore route, Tempest Shield, Surge and Superheat arrive in Phase 2 (Ghornfell, the level-11 power spike). Magical Mending arrives in Phase 3 (Fellhollow). Death From Above! lands between Attack 11 and Attack 30, in Phase 4. Enfeeble arrives in Phase 5 (Umbral Sands).

What this means when you run

  • Unlock Death From Above! at Attack 25 and carry a melee weapon with a plunge animation.
  • Put Magical Mending on slot 1 and Windstep on slot 7, the way Nanobit does.
  • Stock Astral and Law runes for Surge, from the altar or from Garou Packs.

posts.title: What gear and consumables should you bring to a raid speedrun?
posts.html:
The raid speedrun loadout is the short list of items and drinks the record route carries: a Fleet-footed Infusion, Strong Tea, your best mace, a two-handed mage staff and your best mage armour. SamFPlays published it with his skip guide, and every post-1.0.1 route uses it.

What goes in the backpack?

Item Effect How to get it Why the route uses it
Fleet-footed Infusion Sprint costs 50% less stamina for 300 s; +40 hydration 1 Clean Water + 1 Feathers at a Stone or Cooking Range Sprint-heavy route, every split
Strong Tea +20 Rest, +10 hydration 1 Ground Tea Leaves + 3 Clean Water at a Cooking Range Rest restore inside the raid
Best mace Melee, crush damage Smith your best tier Kills the air Garou Thane through the gate
2H mage staff Magic damage Craft your best tier Burns Kuldra's Heart
Best mage armour Magic damage and defence Craft your best tier Heart phase damage check
Leggings of Lightness (optional) Windstep costs 0 runes 6 Coarse Animal Fur + 6 Rune Essence at a Crafting Table Free Windsteps
Antipoison Cures poison Craft or loot Heart phase poison

Recipes and effects come from the wiki pages cited below.

Why is the Fleet-footed Infusion mandatory?

The Fleet-footed Infusion grants the Fleet Footed perk: sprinting costs 50% less stamina for 300 seconds (Fleet-footed infusion, wiki). SamFPlays puts it first: "Fleet Foot Infusion: MUST BRING. Cuts sprinting stamina cost by 50%." (Every Skip Explained, 1:43).

300 seconds is shorter than a 6:50 run. Nanobit re-drinks it in the Stronghold: "Don't forget to re-use your fleet-footed infusion here, because I did." (7:01, 3:22). Carry two.

Infusions share one slot. The wiki's Kuldra strategy page notes they do not stack with each other, so the Fleet-footed Infusion replaces a Pumpkin Spice Infusion (Kuldra/Strategies, wiki).

Why bring Strong Tea?

Strong Tea restores 20 Rest, and inside the raid it is your only rest source: the wiki states "Resting cannot be performed during combat or a raid" (Rest, wiki). SamFPlays rates it "nice to have, restores +20 Rest" (1:43).

Why a mace, a staff and mage armour?

The mace kills the air Garou Thane through the closed gate on Sir_Rebral's Stronghold route. The Garou Thane's weakness is crush (Garou Thane, wiki), which a mace deals. SamFPlays: "Melee weapon: Best mace you have".

The staff and armour finish the run. SamFPlays: "Mage weapon: 2-handed mage staff for killing the heart at the end." and "Armour: best mage gear you have." (1:43).

Pick a jump-attack weapon for the cancels. Nanobit notes the Dragon Scimitar "doesn't have a plunge animation" (7:01, 5:07).

Where do Leggings of Lightness come from?

Leggings of Lightness come from the Suspiciously Light Tattered Boots vestige in a chest atop the Temple Woods windmill (Leggings of Lightness, wiki). Since 1.0, Jagex "replaced it with an ability that makes Windstep cost zero runes to cast while the Leggings are equipped" (1.0 notes, Steam). The trade is zero leg armour.

Which tier of gear do you need?

Power level 7 is the floor. The wiki's Regicide page recommends "Power level 7 or better armour and weapons" (Regicide, wiki). On the Raid Lab Hardcore route that tier comes from Umbral Sands (Phase 5), where the Nightmare Crucibles' Ascension Cores lift your weapon from power level 6 to 7.

Slot Record route Console route Source
Melee Best mace, plus a shield for the Thane Any melee weapon SamFPlays, FastTipsGaming
Magic Best 2H mage staff Fire magic weapon SamFPlays, FastTipsGaming
Armour Best mage armour Not stated SamFPlays
Second melee Dragon Scimitar (rib clip swing) Not used Nanobit

The Thane kill has a fixed rhythm. SamFPlays: "Put on your mace, shield, and then you're going to do the air enchantment just so you attack faster." (Every Skip Explained, 5:38). Enchant Weapon: Air sits at Attack 30.

The Heart has two stances. SamFPlays burns it with the staff from the third line: "The third line here, just stand here, aim for the top of the heart. And left click." (10:40). FastTipsGaming uses fire magic from range: "While inside, my preferred method has always been fire magic." (Fight skip, 1:09). Nanobit uses the melee safespot.

The Dragon Scimitar comes from your first clear: it "can be received after completing the Scorned Wilderness raid and opening the Queenslayer's Reward Pack" (Dragon Scimitar, wiki).

Antipoison is brewed from Irit, Poison Ichor and a Glass Vessel at a Brewing Cauldron (Antipoison Potion, wiki). Carry one for the Heart on the hardcore-safe build.

Nanobit's armour and food are a gap in the sources. His quick-access slots hold his helmet and pies; his armour set is unstated, so match SamFPlays' mage armour.

What this means when you run

  • Carry two Fleet-footed Infusions and drink the second in the Stronghold.
  • Hold a mace for the Thane and swap to the 2H staff for the Heart.
  • Wear a weapon with a plunge animation for every dive cancel.

Sources

  • SamFPlays: "Mage weapon: 2-handed mage staff for killing the heart at the end." (1:43)
  • Nanobit: "Don't forget to re-use your fleet-footed infusion here, because I did." (7:01, 3:22)
  • SamFPlays: "Put on your mace, shield, and then you're going to do the air enchantment just so you attack faster." (Every Skip Explained, 5:38)

posts.title: What should you set up before every raid attempt?
posts.html:
The pre-run setup is the checklist you clear at Rasthin's Rest before you talk to Commander Zilyana: full rest, full hydration, bed spawn, keybinds, settings, a respawned Air Thane and a timer that splits where speedrun.com does.

Every item on it protects stamina, time or a split.

What is on the checklist?

Check Target Why
Rest 100, just slept Low rest caps max stamina
Fresh Start Active (180 s) Rest, hydration and sustenance stop dwindling
Hydration 100 Fastest stamina regen
Bed spawn Rasthin's Rest Deaths return you to the start line
Air Garou Thane Respawned The Stronghold route kills him
Ring keybinds Cancel spell slot 1, Surge 3, Phase Dash 4, Windstep 7 Inputs inside the cancel window
Backpack Two Fleet-footed Infusions, Strong Tea, mace, staff, runes The loadout
HUD and recording HUD visible, game audio on, recording started speedrun.com video rules
Timer Five splits, banner and cut-to-black triggers Matches the speedrun.com rule

How do you set up the bed?

The bed needs 8 ash planks and 4 rough cloth, and "must be under a roof and enclosed with three walls to be used" (Bed, wiki). SamFPlays builds his right at the start: "put a bed right here. Look at that janky roof, put a bed there. That way when you die you respawn right here." (Every Skip Explained, 1:43).

Why sleep right before the run?

Rest caps your stamina. The wiki's thresholds: 50 Tired limits stamina to 80, 25 Knackered to 60, 0 Exhausted to 40 (Rest, wiki). A full night's sleep also grants Fresh Start, a 180-second buff that stops rest, hydration and sustenance dwindling.

Sleep at Rasthin's Rest, then start the run while Fresh Start covers the opening splits. Since 1.0.0.5, "Summon Shelter will be able to be used in the Scorned Wilderness hub" (1.0.0.5 notes, Steam).

Why drink to full hydration?

Hydration sets stamina regen. At 100 hydration stamina regenerates at 6.0 per second; at 0 it regenerates at 0.75 (Hydration, wiki). Drink clean water before entering; dirty water builds toward Soulscourge.

Why check the Air Thane?

The air Garou Thane is a kill on the Stronghold route, and Nanobit found his respawn is slow: "Air Thane takes like 15 minutes to respawn, it's best to just sleep through a night after completing a run... otherwise he doesn't spawn in the next run and ruins your time." (8:32 run, description).

Sleep through a night between attempts. One night covers rest, Fresh Start and the Thane together. Jagex's 1.0.1 notes add that "Obstacles and Enemies now respawn in the Scorned Wildnerness Raid on reset/next run-through" (1.0.1 notes, Steam); check the Thane is standing in the air room before you commit to the gate kill.

Which keybinds speed up the run?

Every spell goes through the ring. The wiki: players "can access their customised spellbooks by pressing the Q-button (default)" (Magic, wiki). Pressing Q then a number picks a ring slot in one motion.

Action Key Source
Spell ring Q (default) Wiki Settings
Cancel spell (Magical Mending) Q 1, then cancel Nanobit
Surge Q 3 loopuleasa
Phase Dash Q 4 loopuleasa
Windstep Q 7 Nanobit
Jump / Double Jump Space (default) Wiki Settings
Evade, Air Dash, Surge charge Ctrl (default); SamFPlays uses Alt Wiki Settings, SamFPlays
Jump Attack Left-click above double-jump height Wiki Settings
Sprint Shift (default) Wiki Settings

Nanobit: "I'm using Q1E for the plunge-cancel tech, and Q7 a lot of the time to windstep. However sometimes it's better to just cast normally if you're doing multiple casts, since you can just spam click to hit the next spell ASAP." (reply on the 7:01). Test what the final E does in your own setup: Dotxy closes the ring with Esc instead.

Number keys without the ring fire quick-access slots. Nanobit: "I find spamming Q3/Q4 just equips my helmet and eats my pies when I don't want to, most of the time." Keep your quick-access slots clear of anything you mind triggering.

Hold sprint once. Nanobit lost time at the start: "Tapped sprint in beginning but was already sprinting, so walked in beginning for about 1.5s before re-sprinting" (7:01, 0:23).

Console layouts are in the console inputs post.

Which settings should you test?

No runner has published their settings. Run each as a test step: change one, run ten attempts of the Fragments zoop, and log the make rate.

Setting Options Test
Frame Rate Limit Dynamic (default), 30, 60, 90, 120, 140 Zoop distance at each cap
KBM Action Direction Camera Facing or Character Facing Which one sends Surge where you aim
Sensitivity X / Y Default 5 Your flight-loop camera control
Visceral Attack Camera Toggle added in 1.0.1 Camera stability during the Jump Attack

Framerate is the strongest lead. Nanobit: "I think lower framerates can give better zoops as well, just from random observations, but I can't/haven't really tested that." (comment on the 7:01). The option list comes from the wiki's Settings page: "Frame Rate Limit: Dynamic (default), 30, 60, 90, 120, 140 frames per second" (Settings, wiki). Lock the cap you choose so every session compares cleanly.

How should your timer and recording work?

Match the speedrun.com rule. The timer starts "the first frame the loading icon disappears going into the raid" and ends "on the frame the screen goes black after the "Get out now!" timer ends after defeating Kuldra's Heart" (speedrun.com Raid rules).

Use the community five-split file: Dragontail Vines, Fragments of Ghornfell, The Shattered Stronghold, Cataclysm Keep, Kuldra's Sanctum. Target splits for a 6:48 run are 1:22.70, 2:23.20, 3:15.70, 4:42.30 and 6:48.10 (Raid Lab run path).

Record full video with game audio and keep the HUD visible: the game rules require "a full video of the run, including game audio" and state that "Dynamic HUD elements should not be obscured or omitted (e.g. health, inventory, stamina)". Start recording a few seconds early. A moderator told ChiefWes: "make sure to start the recording a couple seconds sooner right before you go into the raid." (speedrun.com run).

What this means when you run

  • Sleep at Rasthin's Rest before every attempt to refill rest, start Fresh Start and respawn the air Garou Thane.
  • Bind the ring the way the runners do: cancel spell on 1, Surge on 3, Phase Dash on 4, Windstep on 7.
  • Lock your framerate cap and start recording early with game audio and the HUD visible.

  • What gear and consumables should you bring?

  • Which spells and perks do raid skips use?

Sources

  • Nanobit: "I'm using Q1E for the plunge-cancel tech, and Q7 a lot of the time to windstep." (reply on the 7:01)
  • Nanobit: "Tapped sprint in beginning but was already sprinting" (7:01, 0:23)
  • Nanobit: "Air Thane takes like 15 minutes to respawn, it's best to just sleep through a night after completing a run" (8:32 run, description)
  • Nanobit: "I think lower framerates can give better zoops as well" (comment on the 7:01)
  • loopuleasa: "I spam Q+3 and Q+4 to enable surge and dash" (comment on the 7:01)
  • SamFPlays: "put a bed right here... That way when you die you respawn right here." (Every Skip Explained, 1:43)
  • Jagex, 1.0.1: "Obstacles and Enemies now respawn in the Scorned Wildnerness Raid on reset/next run-through." (Steam)
  • speedrun.com: "All submissions requires a full video of the run, including game audio." (speedrun.com)
  • Wiki: Bed, Rest, Hydration, Magic, Settings

  • One night's sleep at Rasthin's Rest refills rest, grants Fresh Start and respawns the air Garou Thane.
  • Runners bind the cancel spell to Q1 and Windstep to Q7, with Surge and Phase Dash on Q3 and Q4.

posts.title: What is the fastest Scorned Wilderness speedrun route?
posts.html:
The fastest Scorned Wilderness speedrun route is Nanobit's 7:01 route (the fastest run on the 1.0.1 ruleset) with Dotxy's Sanctum flight in the final split. It carries you from the loading screen to the cut to black after Kuldra's Heart in five splits, and it works on patch 1.0.1.2.

This pillar teaches that route one skip group at a time, in the exact order you play it. Every skip names who found it, shows where it happens in a record run, and links the clip.

Why build on the 7:01 instead of the 6:50?

TexasPete's 6:50 is the record to beat and the best movement reference in the game. Its route belongs to an earlier patch: Nanobit says it is "using some strats that have been patched at this point".

Nanobit's 7:01 runs the 1.0.1 route that survives today, with one change he writes into his own description: "Windstepping up the blocks to Kuldra no longer works as of 1.0.1.2/1.0.1.3. You can still get up to that area via just flying lmao." That flight is Dotxy's tech, taught in the Sanctum post.

What are the five splits?

A split is one timed section of the run. The community split file ends splits 1 to 4 on the "EXTRACTION POINT UNLOCKED" banner (the message when you reach a Zilyana Teleporter) and split 5 on the cut to black after "GET OUT NOW!", which is the speedrun.com end rule.

Term What it means
Split One timed section of the run, ended by a fixed on-screen trigger.
Zoop A long launch off an edge that carries you between islands.
Skip A route piece that bypasses the intended path, puzzle or fight.
Sum of best The total of the fastest segment for every split.

Here is every split, measured frame by frame (±0.1 s) in the Raid Lab:

Split TexasPete 6:50 Nanobit 7:01 Faster
1. Dragontail Vines 1:21.52 1:27.82 TexasPete by 6.3 s
2. Fragments of Ghornfell 1:01.10 1:07.10 TexasPete by 6.0 s
3. The Shattered Stronghold 0:51.70 1:03.10 TexasPete by 11.4 s
4. Cataclysm Keep 1:36.30 1:27.80 Nanobit by 8.5 s
5. Kuldra's Sanctum 1:59.38 1:56.15 Nanobit by 3.2 s
Total 6:50.00 7:01.97

TexasPete wins the first three splits. Nanobit wins the Keep and the Sanctum. The fastest segment from each adds up to 6:38.27.

What is the route in play order?

  1. Dragontail Vines: the air anima Windstep, the soulscourge skip and the black dragon skip.
  2. The skip to Fragments of Ghornfell: the zoop past the necromancer area, found by SectorTSWG via Sir_Rebral.
  3. Fragments of Ghornfell: the poison area skip and the Abyssal Demon skip.
  4. The Shattered Stronghold: Sir_Rebral's Garou Thane kill through the gate.
  5. Cataclysm Keep: the hole found by IINo1goodII and notmusty1.
  6. Kuldra's Sanctum: Dotxy's flight, the fight skip and the rib clip.
  7. Kuldra's Heart: where to stand, and the cut to black.

Where is the time left?

Nanobit names the place himself: "Especially in the area with the 3rd BD directly after zooping from keep, if you get a strong enough one you can make it all the way from where you landed to well past the plant."

The biggest open save is the Sanctum. Both record Sanctum segments predate Dotxy's 1.0.1.2 flight, so a clean flight is the clearest path under 6:50.

What is the optimal path on 1.0.1.2?

posts.title: How do you run Dragontail Vines in the Kuldra raid speedrun?
posts.html:
Dragontail Vines is the first split of the Scorned Wilderness raid, from the loading screen to the first extraction point. The 1.0.1.2 route clears it with three skips in a row: the Windstep to the first air anima, the soulscourge skip and the black dragon skip, ending on the jump-off point for the zoop to Fragments.

This is where TexasPete builds his lead. His Vines split is 1:21.52, against Nanobit's 1:27.82, so every dash you save here carries all the way to the cut to black.

What do you need?

Requirement Unlock Used for
Windstep Agility 5 (infobox shows 8) Launch to the first air anima
Double Jump Agility 10 Height on every jump
Air Dash Agility 32 Four dashes to the first pillar
Phase Dash Agility 44 The soulscourge skip
Fleet-footed Infusion Cooking range: 1 Clean Water + 1 Feathers Half-cost sprinting for 300 s

Every unlock is taught in Which Agility levels do you need? and What gear do you bring?.

How do you do the air anima Windstep?

Crystallised Anima is raid scenery you touch to attune to an element for 30 seconds. SamFPlays routes the air charge early so it opens the way ahead.

  1. Sprint from the first frame. Nanobit walked for a moment here and names the cost: about 1.5 s.
  2. Windstep toward the first air anima pillar and chain four air dashes on the way.
  3. Take three air dashes toward the second air anima pillar.

zyneater adds a faster line in his guide description: a better route "directly to the first air anima vent". Watch his 0 to 1 tips and build that line into your practice.

How do you do the soulscourge skip?

SamFPlays names it the "Soulscourge skip (phase dash + food trick)". It carries you past the soulscourge area on a Phase Dash chain.

  1. Follow his line from the explained chapter.
  2. Spend the Phase Dash where he does, and copy his food timing from the original chapter.
  3. I-frame Kuldra's first hit (i-frames: the invulnerable moment of a dash) with a well-timed dash and a tight line over the torch into the first black dragon area, as Nanobit describes.

How do you do the black dragon skip?

The route runs straight past the first black dragon (a power level 8 dragon that every route skips).

  1. Start the Earth Pillar early. Nanobit measures about 1 s here.
  2. Take the clean line down after the dragon to the jump-off point.
  3. Set up the zoop to Fragments, covered in How do you skip to Fragments of Ghornfell?

Does it work on 1.0.1.2?

All three skips work on 1.0.1.2. CrossRSDW's older Dragontail Vines skip from patch 1.0.0.6 (clip) is a research lead: test it three times on 1.0.1.2 before you route it.

posts.title: How do you skip to Fragments of Ghornfell?
posts.html:
The skip to Fragments of Ghornfell is a zoop (a long launch off an edge) that carries you from the end of Dragontail Vines straight into Fragments, skipping the whole necromancer area. SectorTSWG found it on patch 1.0.1, Sir_Rebral spread it, and Nanobit credits both in his 7:01.

It closes split 1 and it comes in two versions: a frame-tight zoop the records use, and an easier zoop into a respawn that Nanobit ran on 1.0.1 day one.

Who found it?

Sir_Rebral writes in his skip video that he learned it from SectorTSWG, and Nanobit thanks "@SectorTSWG via @Sir_Rebral for the new skip to Fragments". SectorTSWG's own run went up on the day 1.0.1 launched, with the note that he "had to find a couple of work arounds".

What do you need?

Requirement Unlock Used for
Double Jump Agility 10 Height off the rock
Air Dash Agility 32 Stretching a short zoop
Phase Dash Agility 44 Recovering a weak zoop
Stamina Fleet-footed Infusion active Dashes at the end of the split

See Which Agility levels do you need? and What is a zoop?

How do you do the fast version?

The fast version is the one in the 7:01. Nanobit calls it "relatively precise" and says half his runs died here, so build it in practice first.

  1. Walk or run to the end of the rock at the jump-off point.
  2. Zoop on the frame you start walking off the rock, or the frame before. Nanobit explains the reason: the rock has "an incredibly small slope after the flat part, before it drops off completely".
  3. Fly straight into Fragments and continue.

Walking gives you more time to react. Nanobit found no distance difference between walking and running.

How do you do the easier version?

The easier version lands you in a respawn past the necromancer area. These are Nanobit's day-one steps, as written in the route:

  1. Zoop across to necro land.
  2. Zoop off the rocks left of the bridge toward the top of the left pillar. It needs height; use one or both dashes depending on the strength of the zoop.
  3. Respawn (the zoop causes it) and continue.

Does it work on 1.0.1.2?

Both versions work on 1.0.1.2, and every 1.0.1 runner uses one of them. SamFPlays marks it NEW in his follow-along.

The target is 12.0 s: TexasPete's 9.5 s line plus a 1.5 s margin. The fallback is Nanobit's zoop started about 1.5 s earlier, around 14.1 s, which costs about 2 s against the target.

The zoop beats the respawn by 24.5 s from the dragon to the fortress courtyard (41.6 s against 66.1 s), because the respawn adds the YOU DIED screen and the wait.

Does TexasPete's direct line still work?

This is a test step. TexasPete leaves the black dragon ledge and goes straight across to Fragments in 9.5 s, a 1.0.0.6-era line that no 1.0.1 runner uses on video yet.

  1. Load his line at 6:50, 1:19 and copy the take-off point.
  2. Try it three times on 1.0.1.2.
  3. Route it when it lands, and keep Nanobit's zoop as the fallback when it fails.

What this means when you run

  • Learn the respawn version first, then switch to the fast zoop once you land it every time in practice.
  • Zoop on the last flat frame of the rock, or the frame before.
  • Test TexasPete's 9.5 s direct line on 1.0.1.2 and keep the zoop as your fallback.

posts.title: How do you skip the poison area and the Abyssal Demon?
posts.html:
Fragments of Ghornfell is the second split of the Scorned Wilderness raid, a Garou courtyard and a toxic castle that ends past the Abyssal Demon (a teleporting demon mini-boss that follows you when you get far away). The 1.0.1.2 route clears it with two skips: the poison area skip and the Surge and Phase Dash past the demon.

TexasPete runs it in 1:01.10 and Nanobit in 1:07.10. TexasPete names this stretch in his commentary: "Where all runs go to die."

What do you need?

Requirement Unlock Used for
Surge Magic 11, 10 Astral + 10 Law runes Three long dodges past the demon
Phase Dash Agility 44, 20 Air + 10 Astral runes Extra air dashes after the Surge
Jump Attack Attack 25 perk "Death From Above!" Plunge cancels
A targeted AoE spell On the spell ring (Q) Powers the dive cancel

See Which spells and perks do raid skips use? and How do you combine Surge and Phase Dash?

How do you skip the poison area?

SamFPlays routes the entire poison area as a skip. His follow-along shows the line and his guide explains it.

  1. Land from the Fragments zoop and follow SamFPlays' line from the explained chapter.
  2. Plunge cancel (cancel the jump-attack animation with a targeted AoE spell) where Nanobit marks it, instead of waiting to fall.
  3. Push into the hole with confidence. Nanobit: more confidence here "will produce better (faster) results".
  4. Zoop hard at 2:32. A strong zoop carries you to his 2:37 spot with zero dashes.

How do you get past the Abyssal Demon?

The demon skip is SamFPlays' Surge then Phase Dash in the air.

  1. Start the Surge from Nanobit's exact spot (7:01, 2:45) so the demon stays in its area.
  2. Surge, then Phase Dash in the air past the demon.
  3. Keep your line clear of the pillar ahead, where a skeleton blocked Nanobit.

notmusty1 posted a full Abyssal Demon skip for 1.0.1 on 17 October (video). Compare it with the Surge line and test it three times on 1.0.1.2 before you route it.

posts.title: How do you skip the Garou Thane in the Shattered Stronghold?
posts.html:
The Garou Thane skip is the route through The Shattered Stronghold that skips the Garou Thane area. The proven 1.0.1 version has you kill the air-attuned Garou Thane through the closed gate with a melee weapon, take his air charge, windjump (a Windstep jump) up to the air door and leave through a hole in the wall. Sir_Rebral found the gate kill, and SamFPlays credits him for it.

SamFPlays calls this "the HARDEST part of the raid". It is the third split, and it is TexasPete's biggest lead: 0:51.70 against Nanobit's 1:03.10.

A faster option arrived on 2 November. FastTipsGaming skips the Thane kill entirely: he climbs the rocks left of the air door, Windsteps and glides over the island into the forest in about 51.9 s. That ties TexasPete's patched climb, so this post teaches the launch first and Sir_Rebral's Thane kill as the fallback.

What do you need?

Requirement Unlock Used for
Best mace you have Melee weapon Killing the Thane through the gate
Windstep Agility 5 (infobox shows 8) The windjump to the air door
Air charge Drops from killing the air Thane Opening the air door
Fleet-footed Infusion Re-drink in this split Sprinting through the Keep

A Garou Thane is a Garou with a tower shield that blocks every attack until its stance breaks. Crush is its weakness, which makes a mace the right tool. See What gear do you bring?

How do you do the no-kill launch?

The no-kill launch is FastTipsGaming's route from his full unedited run of 2 November, played after 1.0.1.2. It needs no air charge and no mace swing.

  1. Climb the rocks to the left of the air door (FastTipsGaming, 4:43).
  2. Windstep from the top (4:59).
  3. Glide over the floating island into the forest (5:00 to 5:19).
  4. Carry on into the parkour toward Cataclysm Keep.

This is a test step. The 51.9 s comes from a tutorial-pace video with no on-screen timer (split point estimated, ±1.5 s). Land it three times on 1.0.1.2, then route it.

How do you do the Thane kill?

The Thane kill is the fallback, proven in the 7:01. These are Nanobit's day-one steps, matched to SamFPlays' chapter:

  1. Pass the water door into the Stronghold.
  2. Kill the air-anima Garou Thane through the closed gate with your mace. Nanobit notes the Thane "likes to walk through the closed gate on his own".
  3. Air-charged, windjump from the tip of the rubble pile up to the air door, and go through.
  4. Exit through the hole in the wall above the orb dispenser.
  5. Re-drink your Fleet-footed Infusion here. Nanobit names this exact moment.
  6. Zoop to the Keep for distance. Nanobit: a strong one needs zero dashes and places you at his 3:57 spot.

Stop swinging the moment the Thane dies. Sir_Rebral watched Nanobit's extra hit after the kill cost the 7:01.

How do you reset between attempts?

The air Thane respawns slowly. On 1.0.1 day one Nanobit timed it at about 15 minutes, so he sleeps through a night after every run. Jagex's 1.0.1 notes say enemies now respawn on reset: check the Thane is standing before you start a timed attempt. The full reset routine is in How do you reset between attempts?

Does it work on 1.0.1.2?

The Thane kill works on 1.0.1.2 and every timed 1.0.1 record uses it. The no-kill launch appears in FastTipsGaming's run of 2 November, after the patch, and waits on a timed run.

The segment runs from the split 2 portal to the split 3 banner in the forest (about ±0.3 s for timed runs).

  • Test FastTipsGaming's no-kill launch three times on 1.0.1.2 and route it when it lands.

posts.title: How do you skip the Cataclysm Keep elemental puzzle?
posts.html:
The Cataclysm Keep skip is a hole in the Keep that drops you out of bounds (outside the playable map) past the elemental puzzle (four pressure pads stepped in the order Air, Water, Earth, Fire). IINo1goodII and notmusty1 found it on patch 1.0.1, and Nanobit used it in his 7:01, thanking them for "a lovely hole in Keep".

Cataclysm Keep is the fourth split, and it is where Nanobit wins: 1:27.80 against TexasPete's 1:36.30.

Who found it?

The credit chain runs through both finders. Nanobit credits "@notmusty1 via @IINo1goodII", and SamFPlays titles his chapter "thank you @IINo1goodII and @notmusty1". Both posted their own videos of the skip on 16 October.

What do you need?

Requirement Unlock Used for
Windstep Agility 5 (infobox shows 8) Parkour and the jump into the hole
Double Jump Agility 10 The rocks at the end of the Keep
Phase Dash Agility 44 Saved for Kuldra when the zoop is strong
Second weapon with a plunge Any weapon except the Dragon Scimitar Plunge cancels

See Which Agility levels do you need? and How do you cancel a jump attack?

How do you do the parkour?

SamFPlays calls this stretch "Parkour section made easy". Follow his line from the follow-along, then add the record details below.

How do you do the Keep hole?

  1. Jump into the out-of-bounds area from Nanobit's reference point (7:01, 4:38).
  2. Land on the first rock and keep moving; the extra jump onto the rock at 4:44 is optional.
  3. Plunge cancel at 5:07 and 5:12 with a weapon that has a plunge animation. Nanobit reminds you the Dragon Scimitar has none.
  4. Use the cancel to dash onto the first rock, then zoop.
  5. Save the Phase Dash for Kuldra when the zoop is strong enough to need only one dash.

What is the backup when the hole fails?

Solve the puzzle fast. Sir_Rebral's advice from before the hole was found still holds: "just solve the puzzle fast with smart pathing." The pads go Air, Water, Earth, Fire, and SuperStooob's guide shows the solution (14:33).

Does it work on 1.0.1.2?

The hole works after 1.0.1.2. FastTipsGaming's full unedited run of 2 November uses the same hole and push-through as Nanobit (FastTipsGaming, 6:25), the first sighting after the patch. Land it three times in practice before a timed run, and keep the puzzle line ready as your backup.

posts.title: How do you fly through Kuldra's Sanctum and skip the fight?
posts.html:
Sanctum flight is Dotxy's 1.0.1.2 way through Kuldra's Sanctum: a loop of jump attacks, each one cancelled by a targeted AoE spell and followed by a fresh jump, that keeps you in the air as long as you repeat it. It replaces the Windstep up the blocks that 1.0.1.2 closed, and it carries you to the fight skip and the rib clip.

Kuldra's Sanctum is the fifth split. Nanobit runs it in 1:56.15 and TexasPete in 1:59.38, and both runs predate the flight. This is the biggest open save in the record.

What do you need?

Requirement Unlock Used for
Windstep Agility 5 (infobox shows 8) Starting the flight
Jump Attack Attack 25 perk "Death From Above!" The plunge you cancel
A targeted AoE spell On the spell ring (Q) The cancel
Surge Magic 11 The bridge to Kuldra
Phase Dash Agility 44 Safety at the bridge

See Which spells and perks do raid skips use? and How do you do the infinite double jump?

How do you fly through the Sanctum?

These are Dotxy's inputs, from his video description:

  1. Windstep.
  2. Jump Attack.
  3. Q (opens the spell ring).
  4. Any targeted AoE spell.
  5. Esc (closes the spell ring).
  6. Jump.
  7. Repeat steps 2 to 6 as long as you need height.

Faster inputs gain height. Dotxy: "If you're faster than I am you can gain height, not just hover". IINo1goodII adds that you can dash and Phase Dash inside the loop, and that he runs it consistently on console.

How do you skip the Kuldra fight?

The Kuldra fight skip takes you past the boss to the Heart. Zilko found the original, credited by Tiger with the Bars; CrossRSDW rebuilt it after 1.0.0.6; SamFPlays teaches the 1.0.1 version; FastTipsGaming showed it working after the latest patch on 27 October and again in a full run on 2 November.

  1. Fly up where the route used to Windstep up the blocks.
  2. Follow SamFPlays' fight-skip line (guide 9:18).
  3. Plunge past the rocks. IINo1goodII describes using "the plunge mech to bypass the rocks on the fight itself since they are patched".
  4. Surge across the bridge, as IINo1goodII does.

How do you do the rib clip?

The rib clip is a clip through the ground at Kuldra's checkpoint. Nanobit credits wes7918 (ChiefWes) for it.

  1. Windjump into the exact spot Nanobit shows at 5:33.
  2. Clip straight through when your position is perfect: Nanobit measures at least 3 s saved over crouch-walking and a sword swing.
  3. Air dash twice after it and keep your Phase Dash for the bridge.
  4. Stay to the RIGHT of the small white floating cube on the bridge.
  5. Spend any Phase Dash you have left at 6:20.

Does it work on 1.0.1.2?

The flight works on 1.0.1.2. Nanobit confirms the old route closed and the new one opened: the blocks "no longer works as of 1.0.1.2/1.0.1.3. You can still get up to that area via just flying". The fight skip is confirmed after the patch by FastTipsGaming. Test the rib clip three times on 1.0.1.2 before you route it.

Ask the moderators before you use a macro. Dotxy invites one for the flight loop, and the rules post covers what to check: How do the speedrun.com raid rules work?

How fast is the Sanctum flight?

The Sanctum segment runs from the Sanctum door load to the Heart tunnel load (the two black loading frames either side of Kuldra's arena), so it holds the flight and the fight skip together.

Dotxy's demo shows 50.6 s from the first Sanctum frame to the tunnel load, plus about 1.3 s of door load. The demo lands and walks the walkway from 0:21 to 0:38, so a direct flight line beats it.

The target is 49.0 s, about 3 s under the demo. This is the swing segment of the record. The flight costs about 17 s against the patched blocks, and a runner on target pace gives back about 6 s of an 8 s lead here. Taking the flight from about 52 s to 49 s is what makes sub-6:50 realistic.

This is a test step. Fly the whole Sanctum without landing, time it from door load to tunnel load, and route it once you reach 49 s three times.

What this means when you run

  • Drill the six-input flight loop until you gain height every cycle.
  • Hold a Phase Dash through the rib clip for the bridge.

posts.title: Where do you stand to kill Kuldra's Heart fast?
posts.html:
Kuldra's Heart is the final target of the raid, inside Kuldra, and the run ends on the frame the screen goes black after the "Get out now!" timer that starts when the Heart dies. The record finish is the melee safespot (a standing spot beside the Heart where you take no hits), which TexasPete brought to the route and Nanobit uses in his 7:01.

The Heart is a DPS check (a fight decided by how much damage you deal per second), and heartworms (parasites with 753 HP that keep respawning in the chamber) guard it. The melee safespot finishes it in about 46 s. SamFPlays' magic spot with a 2H mage staff takes about 92 s and is the calm way to learn the room.

What do you need?

Requirement Source Used for
Melee weapon Your best The melee safespot
2H mage staff Your best The magic spot, from range
Best mage armour Your best Heart damage with magic
Enfeeble Magic 61 Weakening the Heart's attacks
Antipoison Brought in The Heart's poison explosions

See What gear do you bring? and Which spells and perks do raid skips use?

Where is the melee safespot?

The melee Heart is TexasPete's idea, credited by Nanobit. Nanobit slightly missed the safespot at 6:47 in his 7:01 and jumped in correctly at 6:53, about 6 s lost.

  1. Leave the Heart tunnel and jump straight into the safespot along the line Nanobit takes at 6:53.
  2. Burn the Heart from there.
  3. Run for the exit the moment "Get out now!" appears: the timer runs until the screen goes black.

Where do you stand with magic?

Stand back at the edge. Three runners describe the same spot:

  1. Follow SamFPlays' standing spot from his chapter Where to stand so heartworms don't spawn.
  2. Stay up on the edge and cast at the Heart from there. southpark159753: "You can stand back and hit the heart with magic, doesnt start the fight with worms. Like dont drop down into the area."
  3. Hold your spot close to the edge. beandon explains the reason: standing too far in lets a tentacle spawn on you.

How fast is the Heart?

The Heart is timed in two pieces (about ±0.3 s): from the Heart tunnel load to the "GET OUT NOW" banner, then from the banner to the cut to black.

Segment TexasPete 6:50 Nanobit 7:01 TexasPete 7:40 SamFPlays 10:53 Target
Tunnel to Heart dead 47.8 (melee) 46.0 (melee) 53.4 (melee) 91.6 (mage staff) 42.5
Escape to the cut to black 13.8 14.2 14.0 13.9 13.8

The melee safespot saves 45.6 s against the mage staff from range. The target is 42.5 s: Nanobit's 46.0 s with the safespot entered first time. The escape is fixed at about 13.8 to 14.2 s in every run, so the time to gain lives in the Heart itself.

Clip Link
Melee Heart (Nanobit) 7:01, 6:25
Melee Heart (TexasPete) 6:50, 5:55
Mage Heart (SamFPlays) follow-along, 9:07
Where to stand (SamFPlays) guide 10:37
Cut to black TexasPete 6:57, Nanobit 7:26

Does it work on 1.0.1.2?

Both spots work on 1.0.1.2. beandon posted his edge advice on 27 October and southpark159753 his magic spot after the patch went live.

What this means when you run

  • Jump straight into the melee safespot on your first try: that is 6 s against the 7:01.
  • Learn the room with the magic spot at the edge, then switch to melee for timed runs.
  • Run the moment the Heart dies: the escape is a fixed 14 s and the clock stops on the cut to black.

posts.title: What movement tech do you need for the Dragonwilds raid?
posts.html:
Movement tech is the set of movement primitives (short, repeatable input sequences that move you further or faster than the intended path) that every Scorned Wilderness skip is built from. Five primitives cover the whole 1.0.1.2 route: the zoop, the dive cancel, the infinite double jump, Surge plus Phase Dash and the windjump.

The record lives in this pillar. Nanobit names the requirement for a sub-7 directly: the run "needs very clean movement and strong zoops" (7:01 description).

Why does movement decide the record?

Patch 1.0.1 changed the movement kit. Jagex added the Jump Attack and confirmed it works off Windstep: "And yes, Windstep counts here. What goes up, must come crashing down." (1.0.1 patch notes)

The same day, Dotxy turned it into a cancel, and within nine days the cancel became flight. Nanobit sums up the arc: "Plunge-cancel tech has evolved even further" (7:01 description).

The 6:50 predates all of it. TexasPete recorded it "prior to the windstep double jump and some other new routing strats" (6:50 description). The new primitives are where the time below 6:50 comes from.

What are the five primitives?

Primitive What it means Finder Post
Zoop A long launch off an edge between islands, timed to one frame community term; precision notes by Nanobit What is a zoop?
Dive cancel A targeted AoE cast that ends the Jump Attack animation instantly Dotxy How do you cancel a Jump Attack?
Infinite double jump Chained dive cancels and air jumps; through the Sanctum it is flight Dotxy What is the infinite double jump in Dragonwilds?
Surge + Phase Dash Surge dodges chained with extra air dashes for long horizontal distance SamFPlays How does the Surge and Phase Dash combo work?
Windjump and rib clip A Windstep jump onto ledges; a clip through the ground at Kuldra's checkpoint Nanobit, wes7918 What are the windjump and the rib clip?

In what order should you learn them?

  1. Windjump first. It needs only Windstep (Agility 5) and it appears in every split.
  2. Surge plus Phase Dash second. It powers the Abyssal Demon skip and the Sanctum approach.
  3. Dive cancel third. It is the building block of flight.
  4. Infinite double jump fourth. It turns the dive cancel into Sanctum flight, the swing segment of a sub-6:50.
  5. Zoops last. They are the most precise inputs in the run and they repay hundreds of attempts.

What this means when you run

  • Practise the windjump on every ledge you meet until it lands first time.
  • Learn the dive cancel on flat ground before you take it into the Sanctum.
  • Save zoops for last and give them their own practice block every session.

posts.title: What is a zoop in the Dragonwilds raid?
posts.html:
A zoop is the long launch off an edge that carries you from one Scorned Wilderness island to the next, made by inputting the dash on the frame your character walks off the lip. It is the most precise input in the run and the largest single source of time between a 7:01 and a sub-7.

Nanobit puts it at the centre of his run notes: the 7:01 "needs very clean movement and strong zoops. Especially in the area with the 3rd BD directly after zooping from keep" (7:01 description).

What do you need to zoop?

Requirement Unlock Role in the zoop
Air Dash Agility 32 The dash you input at the edge
Phase Dash Agility 44 Recovery when a zoop comes up short
Surge Magic 11 Extra recovery distance
Fleet-footed Infusion consumable Sprint stamina for the run-up

How do you zoop?

Nanobit describes the timing for the hardest zoop in the run, Vines to Fragments:

  1. Walk or run to the end of the flat part of the launch rock.
  2. Watch the lip. The rock has "an incredibly small slope after the flat part, before it drops off completely."
  3. Input the dash "either on the frame you start walking off the rock … or 1 before."
  4. Read the result. "Any earlier and you smash your ankles into the side Fragments and fall to your death, any later and it becomes an air dash."
  5. Walk the approach while you learn it. Nanobit found "walking allows more time to react", with the same distance as running.

Load his Vines to Fragments zoop at 1:45 now and step through the lip frame by frame.

Where does the route zoop?

These are the zoops Nanobit marks as time saves in his 7:01, at video time:

Video time Where Nanobit's note
1:45 Vines to Fragments "Technically could start zoop to Fragments about 1.5s earlier but this zoop is hard, so safety."
2:05 Keep wall across the pond "can make it all the way to the gate with a good one, save maybe 2.5s"
2:32 Fragments "you can make it all the way to where I'm standing at 2:37, with no air/phase dash at all."
3:46 Stronghold "This zoop can go far enough to require no dashes."
3:50 Stronghold to Keep "This saves A LOT of time if it works."
5:18 Keep exit "Sometimes this zoop is strong enough to only need 1 dash, then you can save the phase dash for Kuldra."
5:57 Sanctum approach "With a strong enough zoop you don't need an air or phase dash."

The pattern is consistent: a strong zoop saves the dashes, and saved dashes buy time later at Kuldra.

Is there an easier Fragments skip?

Yes. Nanobit points learners to his slower, safer version: "if you want an easier (but slower) skip to Fragments I suggest checking out my Day 1 Strats Video … for the zoop from necro island into respawn skip" (7:01 comment). The day-one steps read: "zoop left side off rocks left of bridge towards top of pillar on left, needs decent height, may or may not need both dashes depending on strength of zoop" (8:32 description).

The skip itself traces to SectorTSWG via Sir_Rebral: "The skip to Fragments of Ghornfell I saw in a video by @SectorTSWG" (Sir_Rebral, 0:53).

Does framerate change zoop distance?

This is the open experiment of the route. Nanobit: "I think lower framerates can give better zoops as well, just from random observations, but I can't/haven't really tested that." Trance_OCE proposes the test: "see if zooping and distance is tied to FPS (is the case on the tiger engine /destiny 2 and worldlining)".

Run the test yourself: cap your framerate at two values, take 20 zoops from the same rock at each, and mark the landing spot.

What this means when you run

  • Walk the approach to the Fragments zoop until the frame timing feels automatic.
  • Learn the necro-island respawn version first and switch to the direct zoop once it lands every time.
  • Bank every dash a strong zoop saves and spend it at Kuldra.

posts.title: How do you cancel a Jump Attack in Dragonwilds?
posts.html:
The dive cancel (also called the jump-attack cancel, JAC or plunge cancel) is Dotxy's technique for ending the Jump Attack animation instantly: you cast a targeted AoE spell during the plunge and cancel the cast. You land with full control of your character and zero ending lag.

Dotxy posted it on 14 October 2026, the day patch 1.0.1 added the Jump Attack. Nanobit used it in the 7:01 the same week: "Thanks again to @Dotxygaming for the plunge-cancel tech, it's very fun." (7:01 description)

What do you need for a dive cancel?

Requirement Unlock What it means
Death From Above! Attack 25 perk Unlocks the Jump Attack
Height Windstep or double jump The attack triggers "above the max height of the double jump's arc from the ground"; "Windstep counts here"
Targeted AoE spell on the spell ring (Q) The cast that overrides the plunge
Plunge weapon your mace A weapon with a plunge animation

How do you do the dive cancel?

  1. Get airborne with Windstep or a double jump.
  2. Jump Attack. The plunge animation starts.
  3. Open the spell ring (Q) and select any targeted AoE spell during the animation.
  4. Cancel the cast. You have "full movement over your character instantly".
  5. Move, jump or dash straight away.

Watch Dotxy's 51-second demo now and copy the rhythm on flat ground first.

Why does it work?

Since 1.0, casting and movement overlap by design. Jagex: "This means you can opt out of those pesky wind-ups or spells you've committed to mid-combat." (1.0 patch notes) The dive cancel uses that window: the spell cast overrides the plunge, and the cancel overrides the spell.

It works off both jumps. Dotxy: "this works with both windstep and double jumping, any time you're in the jump attack animation you can cancel it".

Where does the route use it?

  • Fragments: Nanobit at 2:13: "Can likely plunge cancel here … instead of waiting to fall, saving a second maybe."
  • Keep exit rocks: 5:07 and 5:12, "as well as using the cancel to dash onto the first rock that I jump from at 5:15."
  • Kuldra's Sanctum: chained dive cancels become flight. See What is the infinite double jump in Dragonwilds?

Which weapon should you hold?

Hold a weapon with a plunge animation. Nanobit: "remember that DScim doesn't have a plunge animation, so you need something else equipped." (7:01 comment, 5:07)

Patch 1.0.1.2 touched the Dragon Scimitar: "Fixed an issue where the Dragon Scimitar would not allow users to Jump Attack in certain circumstances." (1.0.1.2 patch notes) Test the Dragon Scimitar on 1.0.1.2 before routing it; the mace from your gear list is the reliable choice.

What this means when you run

  • Bind a targeted AoE spell to the spell ring before your first practice session.
  • Equip the mace for every section where you plunge cancel.
  • Add the cancels at 2:13, 5:07 and 5:12 once the dive cancel lands every time on flat ground.

posts.title: What is the infinite double jump in Dragonwilds?
posts.html:
The infinite double jump is Dotxy's loop of dive cancels and air jumps that keeps you airborne for as long as you hold the rhythm; chained through Kuldra's Sanctum it is called Sanctum flight. It is the route's answer to patch 1.0.1.2.

This is the swing segment of the record. Both record runs climbed the blocks from the Sanctum door to the heart tunnel in 35.0 s, a route 1.0.1.2 closed. Dotxy's flight demo covers the same stretch in 51.9 s, and the 6:48.10 target pace asks for 49.0 s. Every second of flight you save goes straight off the run.

Why does the route need flight?

Patch 1.0.1.2 closed the old way up. Nanobit: "Windstepping up the blocks to Kuldra no longer works as of 1.0.1.2/1.0.1.3. You can still get up to that area via just flying lmao." (7:01 description)

Dotxy posted flight the same day as the patch: "here's a new way to get through Kuldra's Sanctum quick in the Runescape Dragonwilds 1.0.1.2 hotfix!" (Sanctum flight)

What do you need to fly?

Requirement Unlock Role in the loop
Windstep Agility 5 Starts the loop once
Double Jump Agility 10 The jump at step 6
Death From Above! Attack 25 perk The Jump Attack at step 2
Targeted AoE spell spell ring The cast at step 4
Dive cancel technique Learn it first

How do you do the loop?

Dotxy's inputs, verbatim from his description:

  1. Windstep
  2. Jump Attack
  3. Q (Spell Ring)
  4. [any targeted aoe spell]
  5. Escape (closes Spell Ring interface)
  6. Jump

"Repeat steps 2-6 as needed!" Windstep starts the loop once; steps 2 to 6 repeat.

Speed gains height. Dotxy: "If you're faster than I am you can gain height, not just hover lol" (Infinite Double Jump).

Dashes mix in. IINo1goodII: "btw i'm sure you know you can dash n phase dash doing this too." (comment)

Load the 90-second flight now and run the loop on flat ground until it hovers.

How do you do it on console?

It works on console. IINo1goodII: "I've been doing this consistently on console." brendonboyd7668 shares a PS5 layout:

  1. "Set your spell wheel to where wind step is Triangle R1 input. Set your repair equipment spell to Traingle R2 for Righties or L2 for lefties."
  2. "Start off by practicing this pattern Repair Spell, Cancel spell, double jump R1"
  3. "Add wind step to the beginning of the pattern"

"You don't need to re input windstep after the first time just keep the pattern from Step 2." (comment)

Ask the moderators first. Dotxy suggests one: "Feel free to set up a macro for easy infinite flight!" The speedrun.com raid rules state the timing and video requirements and are silent on macros. Message Archy or dotyoureyes before you submit a run that uses one.

Does it still work today?

Yes, as of 2 November 2026. FastTipsGaming posted "my full unedited Kuldra raid and boss skip in Runescape Dragonwilds" (full raid) using the infinite-jump cycle, plus a tutorial (Infinite Jump EXPLOIT).

posts.title: How does the Surge and Phase Dash combo work?
posts.html:
The Surge and Phase Dash combo is SamFPlays' chain of Surge dodges (three 8-metre dodges from one cast) and Phase Dash (extra air dashes while airborne) that covers long horizontal gaps with almost no stamina. It carries you past the Abyssal Demon and across the Sanctum approach.

SamFPlays opens his every-skip guide with it, in a chapter titled "Phase Dash & Surge Combo" (guide, 0:00).

What do you need for the combo?

Spell / skill Unlock Cost Cooldown What it gives
Surge Magic 11 10 Astral + 10 Law runes 45 s 3 dodges of 8 m, charges last 2 minutes, no stamina per dodge
Air Dash Agility 32 stamina none listed 10 m dash while airborne
Phase Dash Agility 44 20 Air + 10 Astral runes 45 s Extra air dashes, up to 3 per cast

Values are from the Dragonwilds wiki pages cited in the Raid Lab mechanics wiki. Rune and level routes live in Get Raid-Ready.

How do you do the combo?

  1. Cast Surge first. Its three dodges each travel 8 metres, and they cost no stamina.
  2. Jump off the edge.
  3. Chain Phase Dash in the air for the extra distance.
  4. Spend the Surge charges inside their 2-minute window.
  5. Bind both to number keys. loopuleasa: "I spam Q+3 and Q+4 to enable surge and dash".

Watch the Abyssal Demon skip in SamFPlays' run at 3:04 now, then his explained version at 5:00.

Where does the route spend it?

  • Abyssal Demon (Fragments). Nanobit at 2:45: "it's important to start surging from exactly where I do, so the demon doesn't chase you into the next area." notmusty1 posted a full demon skip: "skip the Abyssal Demon completely! Fully working as today 17.10.2026" (video).
  • Keep exit. 5:18: a strong zoop needs one dash, "then you can save the phase dash for Kuldra."
  • Sanctum approach. 5:52: "You can probably air dash at least twice here (don't waste phase dash yet though)"; 6:20: "If you have any phase dashes left, just use them now."

How should you budget the cooldowns?

One cast per spell per segment. Both spells sit on a 45-second cooldown, so plan each cast like a resource.

Nanobit weighs the Surge timing at Kuldra in his 7:04 notes: casting earlier and recasting at the top "could still be faster, and save me a surge from the second side of Kuldra's bridge to her face (instead of jump/dashing), as well as one for the throat" (7:04 description). Test both timings and keep the faster one.

What this means when you run

  • Start the demon Surge from Nanobit's exact spot at 2:45 every attempt.
  • Hold your Phase Dash through the Keep exit and spend it at Kuldra.
  • Bind Surge and Phase Dash to number keys before your next session.

posts.title: What are the windjump and the rib clip in the Kuldra raid?
posts.html:
A windjump is a jump made under Windstep (the Agility spell that raises jump height to 16 metres and slows your fall), used to reach a ledge, a rock or a doorway in one move. The rib clip is the windjump at Kuldra's checkpoint that drops you through the ground at her ribs, found by wes7918 (ChiefWes).

Every split uses a windjump. The rib clip is the single largest movement save in Nanobit's Sanctum notes: "This saves at least 3s."

What do you need?

Term What it means Unlock
Windstep Higher jump, slow fall, 7-second window after the cast, 3 s cooldown Agility 5, 5 Air runes
Windjump A jump taken inside the Windstep window Windstep
Leggings of Lightness Windstep costs zero runes while worn Temple Woods windmill vestige
Rib clip A windjump at Kuldra's ribs that puts you through the ground Windstep, a melee swing as backup

How do you windjump the Stronghold air door?

Nanobit's day-one notes, with the Thane route credited to Sir_Rebral:

  1. Kill the air-anima Garou Thane through the closed gate with a melee weapon.
  2. Take the air charge from the kill.
  3. Windjump up to the air door "from tip of rubble pile and go through".
  4. Exit "through hole in wall above orb dispenser".

Source: 8:32 description. See it in SamFPlays' run at 3:40.

How do you do the rib clip?

  1. Windjump from the rock before Kuldra's checkpoint.
  2. Hit into the ribs at the exact position. Nanobit: "If you're incredibly lucky, or smart enough to figure out the exact position to jump from and hit into, you can clip straight through the ground at rib clip".
  3. Fallback: crouch walk up the rib and swing to clip out, the slower version Nanobit replaces.
  4. Continue to the Sanctum approach.

Watch 5:33 in the 7:01 now, and the swing at 5:38 that loopuleasa called "CHEFS KISS".

Who found the rib clip?

Credit goes to wes7918. Nanobit lists the source in his 7:04 notes: "@wes7918 (Rib Clip at Kuldra Checkpoint)" (7:04 description). wes7918 describes it himself: "i was the one who found the strat to jump on the bone and punch up to get back out into the map" (7:01 comment).

Which windjumps changed with the patches?

Patch 1.0.1 targeted Windstep: "Fixed several Windstep-related skips in the Scorned Wilderness Raid." (Steam) 1.0.1.2 removed TexasPete's rock landing; Keimbho: "the new update made the rock a phantom. Can't land on it anymore." (6:50 comment) Test the rib clip on 1.0.1.2 three times before you route it.

What this means when you run

  • Windjump from the rubble tip to the Stronghold air door every attempt.
  • Practise the rib-clip position until the clip lands without the crouch walk.
  • Retest every windjump after each patch before you route it.
